title: Intentional weekly shepherding notes - Harper Singh
body:
Purpose and framing:
This is my weekly shepherding note — a half-formal, half-scratchpad doc to track the signals I care about, the tiny experiments I'm running to move metrics, and quick retros so I don’t lose context between two-week cadences. Keep it tight: metrics first, blockers second, then hypotheses + next actions.

This week (Mar 2–Mar 8) snapshot:
- Primary focus: increase 'productive deep work hours' from baseline 10h/week -> target 14h/week this sprint.
- Secondary focus: reduce context-switching at lunchtime and late-afternoon (aim: <3x interruptions/day).
- Micro-KPI tracker (raw counts):
  - Deep work sessions (45m+): 8
  - Interruptions logged: 18
  - Meeting hours: 7.5
  - Weekly sprint outputs (docs updated / PRs opened): 4

Signals I’m watching (why these matter):
- Deep work session count: product of schedule discipline + energy.
- Interruptions: leading indicator of scattered attention; drives low-quality time.
- PR velocity: sanity check that deep work time is translating to outputs.
- Mood/energy (self-rated 1-5 each day): 3.6 average this week -> slight dip.

What I tried this week (experiments + quick notes):
1) Buffer blocks: added two 90-min blocks Mon/Wed labeled ‘do-not-disturb — deliverables’. Outcome: started strong, mid-day Slack ping at 11:30 broke flow in Mon. Net deep sessions +2.
2) Lunch quiet policy: no Slack between 12–12:45 and short walk. Outcome: energy bump on Tue/Thu, but forgot Wed. Need more reminders.
3) Meeting merge: collapsed three 1:1 prep threads into single triage doc (linked). Outcome: freed ~30 mins cumulatively, but prep time truncated.
4) Micro-commit rule: if a change can be described in <3 bullet lines, open a PR immediately. Outcome: +2 PRs opened this week, faster review.

What worked well:
- Micro-commit rule is low friction and pushes momentum. Keep.
- Lunch walk improves post-lunch focus, measurable on Wed/Thu energy spikes.

What didn’t work / friction:
- Buffer blocks are too rigid without calendar coordination; I got pings during them. Need shared expectation with immediate teammates.
- End-of-day context shredding: I’m still trying to switch from deep work to async-review mode.

Hypotheses for next sprint (testable):
- H1: A 5-min status card in Slack before buffer blocks (auto-message) reduces interruptions within blocks by 50%. Measure: number of pings inside block.
- H2: A 3-day ritual (calendar + 1 reminder on phone) will increase buffer-block adherence from 50% -> 80%. Measure: fraction of blocks completed without interruption.
- H3: Enforcing micro-commit rule + 1 focused review hour increases PR merge rate by 25% (2-week horizon).

Concrete actions / next week plan (Mar 9–Mar 22 two-week cadence):
- Add Slack scheduled status message (template below) 5 min before each buffer block. (ACTION, owner: me, due: Mar 9)
- Share buffer-block expectation with core collaborators (Ava, Maya) and ask them to respect or re-schedule. (ACTION, owner: me, due: Mar 10)
- Add phone reminder for lunch quiet policy (ACTION, owner: me, due: Mar 9)
- Keep micro-commit rule; schedule 1h review slot Wed afternoon for reviews. (ACTION, owner: me, due: Mar 11)
- Track interruptions with simple tally in Google Keep / timing app; export counts at end of sprint. (ACTION, owner: me, ongoing)

Slack scheduled status template (for buffer block):
- "Heads-up: I'm in a focus block until 1:30pm. If urgent, please DM me with 'URGENT' in the subject and I'll check. Otherwise I’ll respond at 1:30pm."

Data collection plan (minimum viable):
- Maintain two-line daily diary in this doc: energy (1–5) and interruptions count.
- Export counts at end of two weeks -> compute change and decision threshold (if interruptions drop >=30% accept, else iterate).

Retrospective notes (quick):
- Reflection: the small habit changes (walk, micro-commit) had outsized impact vs heavyweight scheduling changes. Lean into frictionless tweaks.
- Emotional signal: I felt more agency when I had visible outputs (PRs) which suggests reward loop matters. Might bias to tactics that yield visible outputs quickly.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Team coordination: Are my buffer blocks harmful to teammates who rely on quick approvals? Need to surface expectations in more places.
- Burnout drift: increasing deep work hours risks fatigue without deliberate recovery planning. Add weekly 90-min recovery slot (reading + walk).
- Measurement accuracy: manual tally for interruptions might be noisy; consider simple phone-based focus app later if noise persists.

Reference links / tickets:
- Personal OKR page: https://confluence.redwood.local/personal-okr-harper-2026
- Related Slack thread: SLACK:#growth - ts:1678912345
- Tiny triage doc for meeting prep: /drive/folders/meet-prep-triage (NOTE: local link)

Quick wins to ship in 48h:
- Post Slack template and schedule messages.
- Turn on phone lunch reminder and do two walks next week.
- Open one micro-PR by Tuesday (practice micro-commit).

Notes to self (loose):
- If irritation spikes during buffer blocks, don’t blame the schedule: log the content of the interruption — is it urgent or trivial? Pattern match.
- Keep language simple when asking teammates to respect blocks; offer clear fallback paths (DM, calendar).

End-of-sprint decision rubric (two-week window):
- If deep work +2 sessions AND interruptions down >=30% -> escalate buffer blocks to default for next sprint.
- If deep work gains but mood drops 0.5+ avg points -> scale back and add explicit recovery windows.


Small snippets / micro-journal (daily entries):
- 2026-03-05: Energy 4, interruptions 2, 2 deep sessions, shipped micro-PR. Mood good.
- 2026-03-06: Energy 3, interruptions 5, buffer block broken once. Lunch walk saved focus.
- 2026-03-07: Energy 4, interruptions 3, merged PR, 90-min deep in AM.

---
Meta: keep this doc as the canonical short-form weekly ledger. Every two weeks I’ll copy into the longer personal OKR page with top-line metrics and decisions. If someone asks for evidence of progress, point them here first.

End.
